text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The High Representative in Bosnia, Carl Bildt, sent a letter to the chairman of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, Flavio Cotti, complaining that OSCE was not fulfilling its tasks in Bosnia.
- The bodies of 12 Bosnian Moslems, who were killed in July 1992 by Bosnian Serb forces, were exhumed from a mass grave in the Sarajevo region on Monday.
- The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), in cooperation with the Soros Open Society Fund, opened a school of journalism in Sarajevo on Monday.

- The leader of Party for Bosnia, Haris Silajdzic, asked the head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, Robert Frowick, to delay local elections in Bosnia until spring next year. Frowick informed him that the final decision will be made this week.
- Bosnia and Jamaica have established diplomatic relations, the Bosnian Foreign Ministry reported on Monday. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
